## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `finished_at` column holds the timestamp of the `started` event. `sources/process_events.sql:4` only allows `created`, `started` and `cleared` events, so no finish event exists to draw from. Running processes therefore show a finish time, and the schema doc contradicts the code. The repository has no tests or dbt data tests that exercise either branch of the new `case` expression.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` copies the start timestamp into a column named and documented as the finish time. With the seed data, process 20 has only a `started` event at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, so it comes out as `state = 'started'` with `finished_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'` even though it is still running. Did you mean to call this column `started_at`? If a finish time is intended, which event type should produce it, given that the source table's check constraint has no finish event? — Anyone reading `finished_at` will treat every running process as finished at the moment it started, which breaks duration, completion and SLA calculations.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — The doc says "NULL means the process has never been started", but the code returns NULL whenever the latest event is anything other than `started`. Process 30 has `started` (event 3) followed by `cleared` (event 4), so its latest event is `cleared` and `finished_at` is NULL even though it was started. Can you either change the sentence to "NULL unless the most recent event is `started`" or change the expression so the column means what the doc says? — Consumers who rely on the documented meaning of NULL will conclude that started-then-cleared processes never ran.

## Strengths
- The one-row-per-process filter (`row_number() … partition by process_id order by event_id desc` with `where recency = 1`) is unchanged, so the new column doesn't change the model's row count.
